A hash function h is a function that maps inputs of arbitrary length (x) to fixed-length outputs (h(x)),
and is fast to compute while being one-way (pre-image resistant) and collision-resistant.
- A one way function: should be able to hash but not "unhash" it.
- it should be collision resistent: two strings shouldnt give the same hash.
Salting of passwords is a method to add some random characters to a password to distinct it from the
real password, so that guessing the hash of common passwords in e.g. rainbow table would be
no because a salt is always random meaning even the same password gives different hash
Many iterations help against attacks because it is more costly for the attacker in terms of time spent
